newsitem.title: FRANCE: NORTH KOREA MAIZE FOOD AID TENDER POSTPONED.
newsitem.headline: NORTH KOREA MAIZE FOOD AID TENDER POSTPONED.

text.p: The European Commission has postponed until August 12 a tender to supply 24,000 tonnes of European Union maize to North Korea as food aid, officials said.

The shipment of maize to famine-stricken North Korea, whose own crop has been devastated by drought in recent weeks, is being organised by the EU on behalf of the United Nations' World Food Programme based in Rome.

Officials involved in the tender declined to say why it had had to be postponed until next Tuesday. But traders said possible reasons included official worries over a 60-day extension clause on deliveries that might encourage speculation between the price of maize (corn) harvested in different years.
European maize is harvested in late September and October.

The World Food Programme said last month it had approved shipments of 130,000 tonnes of commodities worth $45.7 million to feed children. That would bring the total amount pledged by the WFP to $141.5 million.

The agency said donors who had agreed to supply food included the United States, European Union, Ireland, Norway, the OPEC oil producers' cartel and Archer Daniels Midland, a private U.S. grains firm.
The WFP said domestic stocks were almost depleted and it was essential new food arrived before the local October harvest.
North Korea's famine began in 1995 when severe floods destroyed arable land, crops, fertiliser stores and irrigation systems, plunging the country into a dire food shortage.
The recent drought of over 60 days destroyed some 1.5 million tonnes of maize which the country had expected would help cover its needs between November 1997 and October 1998.
